extracted.intended_audience: prospective grantees, nonprofit partners, and philanthropic community seeking Hewlett Foundation funding
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the Hewlett Foundation's mission, grantmaking approach, and program-area priorities that guide which projects and organizations it funds. Useful for prospective applicants to assess alignment with foundation interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — invest in creative thinkers and problem solvers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hewlett Foundation invests in creative thinkers and problem solvers with different perspectives, all working to build an inclusive society where everyone has a meaningful opportunity to thrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding should align with the foundation's core mission of enabling people, communities, and the planet to flourish by supporting creative, diverse approaches that advance inclusion and opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantmaking approach — reliable, responsive, strategic support
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide reliable, responsive, and strategic support to our partners, and promote constructive dialogue across difference to help forge solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation favors partners and projects that benefit from consistent, strategic backing and that engage in constructive dialogue across differences; emphasis on partnerships that help 'make progress possible' and produce tangible benefits to communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide students with rigorous, relevant, and innovative educational opportunities in order to foster mobility and help them contribute to the future of their communities and our country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should focus on rigorous and relevant education innovations that promote student mobility and community contribution; projects that demonstrate evidence of improving educational opportunity and outcomes are implied priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Address climate change globally and conserve the U.S. West to ensure people, communities, and the planet flourish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports interventions that mitigate climate change and conserve natural resources, with particular attention to the U.S. West as well as global climate efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performing Arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Support meaningful artistic experiences for communities throughout the San Francisco Bay Area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is targeted to strengthen performing-arts experiences that are meaningful to Bay Area communities; place-based arts support is a priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender Equity and Governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote gender equity and responsive governance in East and West Africa, Mexico, and the U.S. to foster inclusive societies where everyone can thrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should work on gender equity and governance reforms across specified regions (East and West Africa, Mexico, U.S.) with an emphasis on inclusion and responsive institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen our shared national community through nonpartisan support for our governing institutions to build public trust in a durable democracy where all Americans have a meaningful opportunity to thrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefers nonpartisan initiatives that reinforce institutions, public trust, and democratic durability in the U.S.; proposed work should avoid partisan advocacy and aim to bolster democratic infrastructure and civic inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Philanthropy
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen the capacity of Hewlett grantees, and nonprofits and philanthropy in general, to benefit people, communities, and the planet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports capacity-building, learning, and effectiveness efforts among grantees and the broader philanthropic sector — projects that improve organizational or field-wide impact are aligned with this priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and Society
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and help spread ideas from across the ideological spectrum that will inform what comes next for capitalism in the U.S. and in democratic societies around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for work that generates and disseminates ideas about the future of capitalism and societal-economic arrangements, including cross-ideological research and policy engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Racial Justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote equal opportunity for all by addressing systemic inequalities across issue areas and in society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding priorities include initiatives that confront systemic inequality and expand equal opportunity across sectors and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to opportunities that advance our philanthropic values, incubate new ideas, strengthen our field, and support the Bay Area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flexible funding category is for time-limited or opportunistic initiatives that align with Hewlett's values — such as incubating novel ideas, strengthening the philanthropic field, or addressing urgent Bay Area needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrative examples of impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Using solar power to boost rural Michigan’s economy; Investing in a creative future for California students; Using evidence to improve lives in Uganda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page highlights example projects to show the kinds of outcomes the foundation supports — applicants should consider whether their work produces similar community-focused, evidence-informed impacts.
